title: Check your understanding: Managing Submodule Changes

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of managing submodule changes?
options: Advanced repository features trade simplicity against space, history completeness, performance and tooling compatibility. Select them only after documenting the workflow and recovery path.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Advanced repository features trade simplicity against space, history completeness, performance and tooling compatibility. Select them only after documenting the workflow and recovery path.
questions.explanation: Advanced repository features trade simplicity against space, history completeness, performance and tooling compatibility. Select them only after documenting the workflow and recovery path.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git diff --submodule=log` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with managing submodule changes?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
